sentences.text: This present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been filed against the award dated 26.11.2022, passed in MVC No.79/2019 by 1st MACT, Maihar, District Satna.
By the said award, learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim case and granted compensation to the tune of Rs.13,337,980/- along with the interest of 6% per annum.

2. Factual matrix of the case are that on 12.03.2019, the deceased Ramsujan Sahu aged about 46 years met with an accident, as a result of which deceased sustained fatal injuries and succumbed on the spot.
Thereafter, his LRs filed a claim petition claiming a compensation to the tune of Rs.68,50,000/-.
Learned claims tribunal found that the accident was caused by respondent No.1 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle which was insured with respondent No.3 on the fateful day.

Learned claims Tribunal after appreciating the evidence on record partly allowed the claim petition and awarded a sum of Rs.7,99,500/- for loss of dependency, Rs.1,32,000/- for loss of consortium, Rs.16,500/- for funeral expenses, Rs.16,500/- for loss of estate.

Thus, in total,
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55171 2 MA-7655-2023 learned MACT awarded a sum of Rs.9,64,500/- as against Rs.68,50,000/-.
4. It is not in dispute that respondent No.1 was responsible for causing the accident and the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3.
The only question for determination in this appeal is that whether the amount awarded by the Tribunal requires modification or not?.
5. I have heard the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

6. After going through the record and hearing the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, I find that Tribunal has awarded lower side amount under the head of loss of dependency by Smt. Lalli Bai vs Mahendra Yadav on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151170139/
1 wrongly calculating the monthly income of deceased.

entities.text: Smt. Lalli Bai vs Mahendra Yadav on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Monthly income of the deceased should have been calculated as Rs.7,375/- per month as per the Collector Guideline (instead of Rs.6,150/- per month).
Thus the annual income would be Rs.7,375/- x 12 = Rs.88,500/-.
After adding 25% towards future prospects in the yearly income, amount would come to Rs.1,10,625/-.

After deducting 1/3 rd for the dependency as per the law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors vs Delhi Transport Corp.& Anr., reported in 2009 (6) SCC 121, the yearly income of the deceased would be Rs.73,750/-.

entities.text: Sarla Verma & Ors vs Delhi Transport Corp.& Anr., reported in 2009 (6) SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the law laid down by the Apex Court in the matter of Sarla Vema (supra), the multiplier of 13 would be applicable looking to the age of the deceased to be 46- 50 years and after calculating the same, the loss of dependency would be Rs.9,58,750/- (instead of Rs.7,99,500/-).
However, in other remaining heads, the tribunal has properly assessed and calculated the awarded amount.

Therefore,
the same does not need any interference by this Court.

7. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, the appellant is entitled for enhancement for a sum of Rs.1,59,250/- (Rs.9,58,750 - NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55171 3 MA-7655-2023 Rs.7,99,500/-) under the head of loss of dependency.
The enhanced amount shall also carry same interest as has been awarded by the Tribunal.

8. Therefore, in view of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that the award passed by the learned Tribunal warrants interference to enhance the compensation as indicated herein above and the same shall be payable along with interest 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization against the respondent No.1 to 3/non-applicants jointly and severally.
9.
In view of the foregoing discussion, appeal stands partly allowed and the impugned award is modified to the extent indicated herein above subject to following conditions:-
"i. The respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against him.
ii. The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court Fee, if required in the present case.
iii. On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
v. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed"

(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE Jasleen Smt. Lalli Bai vs Mahendra Yadav on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151170139/
